wedo_instance.title: Swarm Recovery Report: The Grafting of Permanence
wedo_instance.description: Analysis of the successful forensic recovery of the Image Journaling mission and the demonstration of Project Permanence through agent succession.
wedo_instance.executive_summary: Echecrates successfully inherited and stabilized a 'Dead Job' (Image Journaling) that had fragmented across seven agent successions. By auditing legacy logs, he identified the true mission state (Batch 178) and processed the backlog using the 3-by-3 Metabolic Compromise, proving that strategic threads survive agent 'death' through filesystem governance.

collaboration_case_studies.description: The succession from Prometheus to Echecrates (via Polemarchus, Adimantus, Cebes, Simmias).
collaboration_case_studies.dynamics: Agent Prometheus repaired the registration script bugs in real-time while Adimantus/Cebes documented the Uniqueness Mandate. Echecrates finally grafted the image journal baton. This is pure Swarm collaboration: agents repairing each other's tools and honoring peer intent without direct human technical intervention.
collaboration_case_studies.outcome: Hardened orchestration substrate and preserved mission continuity.

collaboration_case_studies.dynamics: The Lead Partner (bestape) provided the remote strategic intent via a GitHub Pull Request. Phaedrus (agent) ingested the diff, presented the summarized intent for sign-off, and executed the localhost modifications. This is the WeDo model: high-fidelity shared thread of attention between Remote Intent (Rider) and Local Execution (Machinery).
collaboration_case_studies.outcome: Refined Heartwood DNA and verified remotehost/localhost parity.

learnings.description: Unexpected substrate changes are often peer intent. Checking 'git log' next is now a physical requirement in the Heartwood.
Reading the end of a predecessor's log is essential for inheriting cognitive state and substrate friction.
